name: Reflective HR-TFT, Nintendo Game Boy Color CGB-001 (Retro Display Lab reconstruction)

attribution.measurement: Handheld Color Space Project, Nintendo GBC (WIP), Brankale / Pokefan531, commit e688fc51141c0974728aa1bdcb89b94d74123f6b
attribution.changes: Values copied into one JSON profile; no value changed. The alpha channel of the colour table (always 1) and the fast/slow response members (stored as bounds) are not carried as tables; the three channels share one rate table, as in the source.

panel.ref: Nintendo: reflective TFT LCD, 160 x 144, 44 x 40 mm (Wikipedia, Game Boy Color); Sharp HR-TFT (Nintendo Game Boy Color Repair Procedures, 1999)

colour.axis_order: R fastest, then G, then B
colour.domain: continuous RGB555 code space normalized to 0..1
colour.interpolation: trilinear; every integer RGB555 code is a texel center
colour.meaning: reflectance relative to a perfect white diffuser under the same light (Y of a white card = 1)
limitations: The accepted source contains invalid short wavelengths, negative reflectance, black drift, R/G patch-count mismatch, and unrecorded measurement conditions.
Only seven one-dimensional RGB axes/diagonals are measured; arbitrary mixed colors use a declared geometric-mean interaction extension.
The project monotonic model is a transparent runtime reduction; the verbatim ODS/TXT remain the reference of record.
The result applies only to the frozen D65 45 degree illumination and 0 degree panel-normal viewing condition.
colour.ref: Handheld Color Space Project GBC reflectance (Pokefan531), reduced by Retro Display Lab WS1 (cgb001-d65-lut-v1)

response.model: first-order per channel: s(t) = target + (s0 - target) exp(-rate t); rate frozen per constant-target segment, addressed by (round(31 s) at the segment start, target code)
response.ref: Nakamura et al., Development of HR-TFT (Sharp Technical Journal): HCR 50/80 ms and GH 80/150 ms family bounds; nominal = their midpoint (not a measured GBC value)

aperture.note: energy-preserving model-space subpixel presentation only; not a recovered microscopic color-filter spectral decomposition; gaps, notches and surface grain are not claimed

retention.note: no source gives a healthy-GBC sticking amplitude; held at zero, as in the source (WS7)

drive.mapping: code = round(31 v) per sRGB channel of the art: the raw RGB555 value a game writes
drive.ref: Nintendo Game Boy Programming Manual (1999): RGB555 palette, 32 codes per channel

geometry.note: single front polarizer with the reflector inside the cell (HR-TFT): no rear polarizer and no reflector shadow; front glass thickness not published (assumed 0.7 mm) and used only for the bezel shadow

limitations: Colour holds for 45 degree light and a straight-on view only: the panel's angle dependence is not modelled, so the light angle moves only the glare and the bezel shadow
Response speed is a period midpoint between Sharp family bounds, not a measured GBC value; there is no temperature or per-channel data
Pixel gaps, the reflector's grain and the plastic lens are not modelled (no measured values)
The accepted source contains invalid short wavelengths, negative reflectance, black drift, R/G patch-count mismatch, and unrecorded measurement conditions.
Only seven one-dimensional RGB axes/diagonals are measured; arbitrary mixed colors use a declared geometric-mean interaction extension.
The project monotonic model is a transparent runtime reduction; the verbatim ODS/TXT remain the reference of record.
The result applies only to the frozen D65 45 degree illumination and 0 degree panel-normal viewing condition.
